input: Learn to solve a Rubik's cube

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether they want to simply solve it once using any method, or master a specific method (e.g. beginner layer-by-layer vs. advanced CFOP), drastically changes the learning path and depth required.
Knowing their current experience level (total beginner vs. partially learned before) determines how much foundational explanation is needed and where the plan should start.
The amount of time they can dedicate per day or week determines how intensive the practice schedule should be and how long the overall plan will take.
Their definition of success — solving it once, solving it reliably every time, or hitting a specific time target — completely changes the end goal and milestones.
Whether they want to learn alone (self-study), follow a specific teacher or YouTube channel, or be guided by a friend affects which resources and formats the plan should recommend.
Whether they already own a cube, and if so what type, determines whether equipment acquisition is the first step and whether the cube they have is suited to learning.
Whether they prefer memorising algorithms step-by-step or understanding the intuitive logic behind moves affects which method and learning style the plan should prioritise.

gold.taskTitle: Learn to Solve a Rubik's Cube
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to learn how to solve a standard Rubik's cube, from their current skill level to being able to complete a full solve.

questions.title: Which solving method do you want to learn?
questions.description: Do they want a simple beginner method (e.g. layer-by-layer) to just get it solved, or a more advanced method like CFOP used by speedcubers?

questions.title: What is your experience with the cube so far?
questions.description: Are they a complete beginner who has never solved it, someone who partially learned before, or someone who can solve one or two layers already?

questions.title: How much time can you practise each day?
questions.description: Understanding their available daily or weekly practice time shapes the intensity and duration of the learning schedule.

questions.title: What does success look like to you?
questions.description: Do they want to solve it just once, solve it consistently every time, or reach a specific time goal like sub-2 minutes or sub-1 minute?

questions.title: Do you prefer learning alone or with guided help?
questions.description: Would they rather self-study with written guides, follow along with YouTube tutorials, or learn with a friend who already knows how to solve it?

questions.title: Do you already own a Rubik's cube?
questions.description: Knowing whether they have a cube — and what kind — determines if sourcing equipment is a first step and whether their current cube is suitable for learning.

questions.title: Do you prefer memorising algorithms or understanding the logic?
questions.description: Some learners prefer step-by-step algorithm memorisation, while others want to understand why each move works — this shapes which method and resources to recommend.
